$comment: Safari's own MCP server — `safaridriver --mcp`, shipped inside macOS.
Apple added it in Safari Technology Preview 247 and it is live in the Safari 27.0 that
ships with this macOS 27 beta (`safaridriver --help` lists --mcp). 17 tools, stdio.
Nothing to install and no supply chain: no npm package, no driver, no cask. It is the
same safaridriver that has always shipped with the OS, run in a different mode.
⚠ It needed no `safaridriver --enable` here — verified 2026-09-02 by driving a real
session cold. If a session ever fails with `Could not create a session`, that is the
command to run (it prompts for authentication, so it is yours to run, not an agent's).
⚠ OFF BY DEFAULT, deliberately — 17 tool descriptions in every session to serve a rare
one is the wrong trade, exactly as for firefox-devtools. Load it per session:
claude --safari           (the wrapper passes --mcp-config with this file)
Drives an isolated WebDriver automation session, not the logged-in Safari — so it is the
safe one to point at a page, and the wrong one for anything needing your cookies.
⚠ Closing the window out from under a live session leaves the server with no addressable
browsing context: navigate_to_url still reports success, list_tabs then returns [] and the
next evaluate_javascript fails with `Could not find browsing context`. create_tab recovers
it. Observed 2026-09-02 — the cause was a human closing the window, not a Safari defect.
WebGPU works headed and out of the box: vendor `apple`, timestamp-query,
texture-compression-bc, maxTextureDimension2D 16384 (Firefox reports 32767 — a real
cross-browser limit difference, not a reporting artifact).
